description: An index advisory spec defines a set of index add/remove/retain actions with justifications, ensuring indexes are purposeful, non-redundant, and do not over-burden write-heavy tables.

rules.description: The spec must declare an indexes array. Each entry must have table, action (add/remove/retain), and columns (for add/retain).
Every add index action must have a rationale field of at least 20 characters explaining the specific query pattern it supports. Vague rationales (performance, speed, optimization) are rejected.
After applying add and remove actions, no table may have more than 10 total indexes without index_limit_waiver: true and a documented justification. More than 10 indexes degrades write performance.

No two add or retain entries on the same table may cover identical columns. Prefix-redundant indexes (A when A,B exists) are also flagged. Use redundant_ok: true only for indexes with specific predicates or includes.

Tables declared write_heavy: true may receive at most 3 new index additions without write_heavy_index_waiver: true plus justification. Each additional index on a write-heavy table increases write latency linearly.
Every remove index action must have a reason field of at least 15 characters. Recreating a dropped index on a large table takes hours — removal must be documented and auditable.
